title: CRLA/110/2011 of KISHAN SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No. 110 of 2011
Kishan Singh ........Appellant.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. .......Respondents
Mr. U.S. Bhakuni, Advocate (Amicus Curiae) for the appellant.
Mr. Vinod Sharma, Deputy Advocate General with Mr. Vijay Khanduri, Brief
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand / opposite party.

Coram : Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C. J.
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Barin Ghosh, C.J. (Oral)

In the instant case, appellant was charged for having
committed offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376 of the
Indian Penal Code. He has been convicted by the judgment under
Appeal for offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC. The
sentence is life imprisonment and a fine of `10,000/-. In the instant
case, appellant was arrested by the people of the locality a few
yards away from the place of incident. The incident alleged was
rape of a four-year-old female child. Devendra Singh, who
deposed as PW1 and who recorded his statement under Section 164
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, is the man behind ultimate
arrest of the appellant. According to the evidence, he saw from a
few feet above that a person is in half-necked condition. PW1,
therefore, threw a few pebbles toward that half-naked person
thinking that the person will dress himself properly and go away
form the place. The person concerned, however, neither dressed
himself properly nor left the place. PW1, accordingly, jumped
down for the purpose of finding out what the half-naked person
was doing. He saw that the half-naked person is committing rape
upon the victim and has silenced the victim by putting his hands on
her mouth. PW1, accordingly, shouted "what are you doing".

2
Sensing that PW1 has arrived, that person started running. PW1
saw the victim lying with blood all around, but he chased that
unknown person. Ultimately, a few yards away therefrom, PW1
could hold the legs of that unknown person. By that time, many
others had come. PW1, then, returned to the victim, picked her up
and took her to the hospital. Later, the family of the victim came to
learn about the incident while the unknown apprehended person
was arrested and the father of the victim, Himmat Singh (PW3)
lodged the First Information Report. In course of investigation,
victim was medically examined when no spermatozoa was found
present in her vagina, but it was found that she has been brutalized
in her private parts and, also, in her vagina by some blunt object.
The Medical Officer, who examined the victim, opined that rape
cannot be ruled out. It was found that vagina was bleeding
profusely. The Medical Officer reported that the age of the victim
was less than five years. The soil, where the incident had,
allegedly, taken place and the soil found from the clothing of the
victim were sent for examination and they matched. The T-shirt of
the victim, pajami of the victim, pantaloon of the accused, shirt of
the accused, underwear of the accused, handkerchief of the
accused, amongst others, were seized and sent for examination.
Blood sample of the accused was also taken and it transpired that
his blood was of 'AB' group. It transpired that the shirt of the
accused was stained with his own blood. It transpired that human
blood group 'A' was found on the pajami of the victim and on the
underwear of the accused. Medical examination of the appellant
was also done, when it transpired that he has received several
bruises, most of which were of minor in nature and suggested to
have received while he jumped from upper layer to lower layer in
order to escape from PW1. The principal evidence, in the instant
case, was tendered by PW1 and the same was supported by the
scientific evidence discussed above. Having considered those
evidences on record, the Court below, by the judgment under
Appeal, convicted the appellant.

3
 2. Before us, learned Amicus Curiae submitted that PW1
was not an eye-witness to the incident. It was submitted that PW1
was several yards away from the place of incident according to his
own showing. It was submitted that the appellant, a constable, was
framed. It was, however, not submitted how the appellant was
framed. No doubt PW1 was away from the appellant when PW1
for the first time noticed the appellant in half-naked condition.
According to PW1, he warned the appellant by throwing pebbles
towards him. Appellant, according to PW1, did not pay any heed
thereto. According to PW1, that compelled PW1 to reach the place
of incident, when, according to PW1, he saw that the appellant is
committing rape on the victim. Soon thereafter, appellant was
chased by PW1 and that resulted in his arrest. Pajami of the victim
and the underwear of the appellant contained group 'A' of human
blood, whereas the blood group of the appellant was 'AB'. Semen
was detected in the pajami, vaginal swab, two glass slides having
vaginal smear of the victim as well as in the shirt, underwear, swab
culture specimen from glans and corona and pubic hair of the
accused. The testimony of PW1, in the instant case, was
corroborated by the medical evidence.
 3. That being the situation, there cannot be any doubt
that the appellant is guilty of commission of offence of rape upon a
female child of less than five years old. Conviction, accordingly, is
not interferable. Having regard to the nature of the crime, there is
no scope of interference with the sentence awarded. The Appeal
fails and the same is dismissed.
 4. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the Court below
along with the lower court records.
